findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file is missing, empty, or unreadable
findings.failure_mode: entire process aborts on missing config/session file instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle gracefully
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>, use map_err on fs::read_to_string, and define a LoadError::Io variant

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds I/O (stdout) inside the parsing/mapping logic
findings.failure_mode: pure calculation is contaminated with side effects; output order becomes nondeterministic relative to parsing; caller cannot suppress diagnostic output without killing all stdout
findings.fix: remove println entirely; move all diagnostics to the shell boundary (caller or action layer); if a log is needed, pass a sink callback or return a diagnostic enum alongside records

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the first element by unchecked indexing into a split-derived Vec
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with no comma panics at runtime via index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) to get (_name, value_str) safely, then access only validated fields

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the second element by unchecked indexing into a split-derived Vec
findings.failure_mode: malformed line with only one field panics at runtime via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') as the sole parse primitive; it yields exactly two fields or an error

findings.failure_mode: a single corrupted line (e.g. 'name,abc') aborts the entire session load instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use .map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(e.to_string())) on the parse call and propagate Result

findings.problem: as u16 cast after parse::<u32>() silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a legitimate 32-bit value like 70000 wraps to 4464 silently, corrupting data with no error or warning
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: load_sessions fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), stdout I/O (println), parsing, allocation, and domain construction into a single 15-line function
findings.failure_mode: violates Data/Calculations/Actions architecture; pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested without a filesystem; shell and core are inseparable
findings.fix: extract a pure parse_line(input: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> function; have load_sessions call parse_line inside the iterator; keep file I/O confined to the action layer

findings.problem: raw String and u16 primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid domain states directly via Record { name: String::new(), value: 0 }
findings.failure_mode: illegal states like empty names or zero values are representable; domain invariants have no enforcement point
findings.fix: define newtype Name(String) with a parse constructor that rejects empty/whitespace names; define value validation at construction; make Record::new(...) the only public construction path

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a full Vec<String> for every line when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation per line; with hostile input (many commas) the Vec grows unbounded
findings.fix: replace with line.split_once(',') which yields exactly two &str references with zero allocation; no Vec needed for fixed-arity lines

findings.problem: load_sessions collects all records into Vec<Record> with no max_items cap, no try_reserve, and no input size validation
findings.failure_mode: a large or unbounded file causes uncontrolled heap growth; memory exhaustion or OOM without graceful degradation
findings.fix: accept max_items: usize parameter; call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? after cap validation; enforce per-line count; return typed Allocation error

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no Result; all failures are panics with no typed error taxonomy
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot distinguish IO errors from parse errors from validation errors; no recovery strategy is possible
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> where LoadError is an enum with variants: Io(std::io::Error), Invalid(line description), Overflow, Allocation

findings.fix: add a criterion or custom benchmark with workload definition, baseline measurement, and regression threshold
